main_body: Grey stone forge: a chimney hood block on top, a stone wall front with an arched fire opening full of flames, and a lighter stone ledge below. It is drawn flat from the front.
top_band: none. Column x=16 shows an outline at row 0, then grey L=137 at rows 1-3, which is the inside of the hood's front panel, then a light edge at row 5 and the same mid-grey (L~103) face below. No horizontal surface is visible from above.
evidence: The whole forge is a front elevation. The chimney hood is a flat rectangle panel with a thin light line at row 5, and the stone wall, the fire mouth and the ledge are painted flat on the front plane. Fire fills the opening and there is no roof or top slope. The hood top is not a surface seen from above, and the grey L=137 rows 1-3 are the same tone family as the face (difference under 25 L from some face rows). The ledge at row 25 is a 1-row line. Nothing reads as a top surface under the 3/4 contract, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 16 distinct colours against 185 and 66 for the references, though its median of 15 colours per tile is close to the references' 18 and 11. The stone has about 3 grey steps and the fire has about 5 warm steps, so the shading is shallower than the roof and wall ramps of the references. 81% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline reads as near-black, which is the sticker look. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the stone checker and the flame dots give some texture, but it is still less rich than the references.
